title: Halifax Indigenous Glass Art Workshop and Museum Entry
includes: • Plan for an additional 60-90 minutes to enjoy the full museum experience
• All workshop materials provided including safety equipment, tools, and instruction
• Indigenous DIY Mosaic Art Kit to take home
requirements: Infants and small children can ride in a pram or stroller
All areas and surfaces are wheelchair accessible
Suitable for all physical fitness levels
Guests should be comfortable with a short, approximately two-minute indoor walk between the classroom and the museum exhibit. The route is accessible.
cancellation: For a full refund, cancel at least 24 hours before the scheduled departure time.
blurb:
• Three Experiences in One — Combine museum admission, a private artist-led tour, and a hands-on Mosaic Glass Art workshop in one meaningful experience.

• Meet the Artists — Speak with the First Nations glass artist family behind - Welcome to Turtle Island - and hear the stories behind the installation.

• Explore Indigenous Knowledge — Learn national Indigenous perspectives through the powerful immigration lens of Pier 21.

• Discover Mi’kmaw Nationhood — Learn about Mi’kma’ki, the Mi’kmaq as the First Peoples of this land, and Mi’kmaw communities across Nova Scotia and the Atlantic region.

• Create with Glass — Make your own artwork while learning a hands-on mosaic glass technique in a medium where Indigenous artists are rarely represented.

• Engage with Culture — Participate in ceremony, cultural teachings, personal storytelling (Anishinaabe, Anisinew, Mi’kmaw Nations).

• Feel Welcome — Enjoy a welcoming, accessible, family-friendly experience on Halifax’s historic waterfront.
